# KyberNow

> KyberNow is free, open-source (AGPL-3.0) remote play and remote desktop: install KyberNow Station on your Windows PC or your Apple-silicon Mac, then play and work on it from all your devices with KyberNow Link, in a native app or in a web browser. The same apps also play a PS5 or PS4 on your network, and KyberNow Share lets guests watch or play with you and lets you lend the computer to family, friends or a team. It is an alternative to Sunshine + Moonlight, built on the Kyber streaming engine (by VLC developers) and the QUIC protocol. Currently in beta (0.x versions, not yet 1.0).

Key facts:

- **What it is**: self-hosted, "your own cloud". Unlike cloud gaming services, nothing is rented. At home the picture goes straight from the PC to your devices, with no server in between. Away from home, your devices reach the PC through KyberNow's relay (an Admin setting, "Access away from home", off by default; the public relay share.kybernow.app is open to everyone, and you can install your own) or through a VPN (Tailscale, WireGuard); the PC must be switched on. In the apps, the picture, the sound and the keystrokes stay encrypted end to end through the relay, which sees addresses, bitrates and share codes; a browser is the exception, as the relay decrypts its traffic to forward it.
- **Latency**: 9.4 ms median from capture to display, measured on 19 October 2026 with the Kyber 0.29 engine and its own client (RTX 3080 Ti PC to a MacBook Pro M4 Max, local network, H.264). With KyberNow's virtual display at 3840 × 2160 and 160 Hz, the median measured the same day was 8.3 ms; about 10 ms with the Windows app.
- **Out of the box**: a virtual display at each device's resolution and refresh rate (checked up to 3840 × 2160 at 160 Hz), the PC's own screens turned off during the session and back on at the end; sound in stereo, 5.1 or 7.1 depending on the device (Steam must be installed on the PC for its virtual speakers); variable refresh rate on Mac, Windows, Linux and Android phones; shared clipboard on desktop and mobile apps; 4:4:4 colour for sharp text on devices that decode it; up to four controllers, seen by the PC as Xbox controllers.
- **Resilience**: every app reconnects on its own after a network drop (ten attempts, one second apart); losses are corrected (forward error correction in the Game and Max profiles) and native apps ask for a full picture after a loss.
- **Controllers**: in KyberNow Admin, each device can have an app that opens on the PC when its session starts (Steam Big Picture, Playnite, Xbox, Epic, GOG and others are detected), closed at the end. The TV apps (Apple TV, Android TV, LG), the Steam Deck and KyberNow Link OS are navigated entirely with a controller, which can also act as a mouse on the Windows desktop; on Mac and iPhone/iPad the controller opens the session menu (L1 + R1 + Start + Select).
- **KyberNow Share**: share the computer with up to four guests, from the session bar or from the computer itself (choose the screen to show and keep using it). Guests join with a six-digit code, a link or a QR code, in a KyberNow Link app or in a browser, at home or from afar through the relay (the host accepts each guest who comes from the internet). A guest arrives as a spectator; the host gives them, separately, their controllers and the keyboard and mouse, and the Station enforces these rights. Each guest picks their own picture quality (Auto, same as the host, 4K 60 Hz, 1080p 60 Hz, 720p 30 Hz), never above the host's, without ever disturbing the host's picture. Dedicated page: https://www.kybernow.app/en/share/
- **Lending the computer** (part of KyberNow Share, since 0.9.0): hand the computer to someone while you are not using it, a relative who enjoys your gaming PC or a colleague who needs the workstation. Three ways: a six-digit code for one session (1, 2 or 4 hours, or until you take it back; the code is used once and valid 24 hours), friend accounts created in Admin (username, password, invitation link; the friend borrows when the computer is free, otherwise asks), and weekly time slots (during their slot the friend goes before the host, with 2 minutes' notice). The borrower plays or works from their own device in "console mode": a full-screen launcher that only shows the allowed apps (any app from the Start menu: game launchers such as Steam in Big Picture, Epic, GOG or Playnite, a single game, a work program), with the Steam account chosen per loan (theirs, with Steam family sharing, or the host's). Explorer, the Windows key, Alt+Tab, Task Manager, command prompts, Open/Save As dialogs and apps outside the list are blocked; a game can still read the disk, so lend to people you trust. The host takes the computer back with a 2-minute notice; afterwards apps close, Steam returns to the host's account, windows come back and the Windows session locks. One loan at a time; the borrower can come back for 15 minutes after a dropped connection.
- **HDR** (since 0.9.1): on an HDR screen (a Mac's XDR display, an iPhone, an iPad, an HDR TV behind an Apple TV, an LG TV) an "HDR" chip on the computer card is on by default and remembered per computer; HDR games and Windows arrive as they are (HEVC Main 10 or AV1 10-bit, 4:2:0); the Station switches the virtual display to HDR at the start of the session and back at the end, and tells games the brightness of the device's screen; an "HDR calibration" screen offers four test patterns; a share guest without an HDR screen gets an SDR picture. Needs Windows 11 24H2 and a graphics card with a 10-bit encoder on the PC; a Mac Station does HDR with the Apple chip. Android, Windows and Linux apps: later.
- **PlayStation consoles** (since 0.9.5, all KyberNow Link apps): a PS5 or PS4 on your network appears on the home screen next to your computers, like Sony's Remote Play. Pair once with the 8-digit code shown by the console (Settings › System › Remote Play › Link Device) after signing in to the PlayStation Network account once (several accounts per device, several accounts per console); "Play" or "Wake and play"; picture up to 1080p at 60 fps (upscaled with adjustable sharpness on Apple devices), HDR on an HDR screen; full DualSense (adaptive triggers, rumble, touchpad, gyroscope; HD haptics over USB on Mac), keyboard and mouse standing in for a controller with a configurable layout; accounts and consoles follow Apple devices through iCloud and are sent to a TV or PC with a 6-digit code. Away from home through a VPN (add the console by address) or through the KyberNow relay with a Station switched on at home on the console's network; never through Sony's servers. KyberNow is not affiliated with Sony.
- **Three products**: KyberNow Station (on the Windows PC or Mac that streams), KyberNow Admin (the Station's settings, in the browser) and KyberNow Link (the apps that display the PC on your devices). "KyberNow" alone is the name of the whole project. Former names: KyberNow Server (now Station), the KyberNow console (now Admin), the KyberNow apps or clients (now Link).
- **KyberNow Station**: Windows 10 or 11, any graphics card (NVIDIA, AMD, Intel, eGPU) or the processor. One installer (KyberNow-Station-Setup.exe) sets up the Kyber engine, KyberNow Admin, a virtual display and virtual speakers per session, the controller driver and the firewall (two ports chosen at install, plus local discovery). No online account: a local name and password chosen at install; devices pair with a six-digit code accepted in Admin. **KyberNow Station for Mac** (KyberNow-Station-Mac.dmg, signed and notarised): an Apple-silicon Mac on macOS 15 or later becomes a Station like a Windows PC, with the same Admin, a virtual display at each device's resolution (the Mac's screens off during the session), a KyberNow sound output (stereo, 5.1, 7.1), HDR, sharing and lending, updates from Admin; three macOS permissions at install (Screen Recording, Accessibility, Microphone for the virtual sound output); from a PC or TV the Windows key acts as ⌘ and the Keys menu offers the Mac combinations and "Ctrl acts as ⌘".
- **KyberNow Link**: your computer on all your devices. Native apps for Mac, Windows, Apple TV, iPhone, iPad, Android 11 or later (phones, tablets, Android TV and Google TV), LG TVs (webOS 5 or later, installed in developer mode), Linux (desktop, Steam Deck, SteamOS in the living room, as a Flatpak) and the Raspberry Pi (Pi 3, 4 and 5, as a .deb on 64-bit Raspberry Pi OS, or as **KyberNow Link OS**, an image written with Raspberry Pi Imager that boots straight into Link, with HDMI-CEC and whole-OS A/B updates on Pi 4 and 5). Apple TV and iPhone/iPad apps are installed from a Mac with Xcode for now. The Steam Deck and Raspberry Pi versions have not yet been tried on real hardware. A web version served by the Station itself works in a modern browser (stereo sound).
- **Versus Sunshine + Moonlight**: QUIC (RFC 9000) instead of GameStream; picture always encrypted; virtual display at the device's resolution built in; pairing through Bonjour, QR code or an on-screen code instead of a PIN; works in the browser too; HDR; guests and lending; relay for away from home; PlayStation consoles.
- **Price**: free, no online account, no subscription, no ads. Community, non-commercial project by Les Lignes Claires. Not affiliated with or endorsed by the Kyber team.

## Pages

- [Home (English)](https://www.kybernow.app/en/): presentation video, the computer on each device in everyday situations, PlayStation consoles, what you need to get started, the three products (Station, Admin, Link), KyberNow Share in short, what KyberNow sorts out for you (HDR included), a short FAQ, downloads
- [KyberNow Share (English)](https://www.kybernow.app/en/share/): playing together with up to four guests, lending the computer to family, friends or a team (codes, friend accounts, time slots, console mode), away from home through the relay, a Share FAQ
- [Technology (English)](https://www.kybernow.app/en/technology/): the measured trip of a picture, QUIC, the Kyber engine, comparison with Sunshine + Moonlight, features and profiles in detail
- [Guide and FAQ (English)](https://www.kybernow.app/en/guide/): installing KyberNow Station on a Windows PC or a Mac, connecting a Mac, a Windows PC, an Apple TV, an iPhone or iPad, an Android device, an LG TV, a Linux PC, a Steam Deck or SteamOS, a Raspberry Pi (KyberNow Link OS or the app), or a browser with KyberNow Link, sessions and HDR, playing your PlayStation, sharing with someone (KyberNow Share), lending your computer, away from home (KyberNow's relay or a VPN), installing your own relay, updates, uninstalling, frequently asked questions
- [Accueil (français)](https://www.kybernow.app/): the same home page in French
- [KyberNow Share (français)](https://www.kybernow.app/share/): the same Share page in French

- [Guide et FAQ (français)](https://www.kybernow.app/guide/): the same guide in French
